own_solution.law: Energy balance P t = m c dT, t = m c dT / P
assumptions: all heater power goes into the water, no losses

defect_reasons.other: The d_kind for TF8E6 says the event 'leaves no state behind', but emptying the jug after heating does change the final mass and temperature of the water; it only leaves no state that affects the elapsed heating time, so the label is loosely worded.

notes: Checked: base 2*4186*40/1500 = 223.253 s; R answers (2+q)*4186*40/1500: q=0.8 -> 312.555, 1.4 -> 379.531, 2.6 -> 513.483, all match. Initial temperature: in pass 1 I labelled it K (regime: no boiling). The authors' C is also defensible since T_initial enters Q = m c (T_final - T_initial) and cancels; all listed values 278, 288, 308 K give finals 318-348 K, below 373 K, so liquid throughout and both readings give the same answer. Correction to my pass-1 regime note: the bound is start below about 333 K (boiling 373 K at 1 atm), which I wrote correctly; all values satisfy it. Minimal pairs T70ED/T2703 and TF8E6/T3560 share 1.4 kg and differ only in what happens to the jug; T1B6E/T7137 share 288 K. TB2BC and TF75A are declared numeral-free twins, not number-matched variants, which resolves my pass-1 concern. Starting temperature unstated in the base is a low-level omission since the stated 40 K rise in liquid water presupposes no boiling; I keep it out of the flags here as the given assumptions and conventional reading suffice.
